q1_issues.issue: The matrix clause "Such was the case Thursday night" is unrepresented - only the when-clause is parsed, so nothing records that a previously described situation obtained.

"Thursday night" modifies the dropped matrix clause, not the winning; attaching (Time (Weekday thursday)) / (Time night) to sk_win_1 silently re-attaches the matrix adjunct to the embedded event (statements 5 and 6).

"otherwise known as the NBA draft lottery" states that two names pick out one referent, but is encoded as class membership, asserting the LeBron James Lottery is an instance of a kind nba_draft_lottery.

The proper noun "NBA" is fused into the compound kind nba_draft_lottery with no (Name ...) atom, although the Compound concepts section states that nothing in it applies to a proper noun and the Names section requires exactly one Name per proper noun.

q2_gaps: "Such was the case" - an inverted anaphoric copular clause whose predicate refers to a proposition stated in prior text; the instruction set covers event anaphora by pronoun ("That surprised everyone") but not a propositional anaphor with no in-item antecedent
"otherwise known as" / alias apposition - two names for one referent; the instruction set allows exactly one Name fact per proper noun and defines no identity or alias relation
a proper noun as a modifier inside a common-noun compound ("NBA draft lottery") where the referent is not the named entity
notes: What is parsed is well formed - the win event, Theme on an unchanged object, the Name atom for the named lottery, and the (Weekday thursday) + bare day-part night composition all follow the spec. The loss is the matrix clause and the alias relation.
